column1: `tr`: what does it operate on, what's its I/O model, and how does `tr SET1 SET2` map (vs sed)?
column2:
Translate/delete/squeeze CHARACTERS. It's a FILTER: reads STDIN -> STDOUT, takes
NO filename args (pipe or redirect:  tr . - < file ).

tr SET1 SET2 maps each char in SET1 to the SAME-POSITION char in SET2:
  echo abc | tr abc xyz  ->  xyz    (a->x b->y c->z; three 1:1 maps, NOT "abc"->"xyz")
No regex / multi-char patterns — that's sed. SET2 shorter -> its last char repeats
(tr a-z x maps all lowercase to x).

-d SET   delete chars in SET       (tr -d '\n' strips newlines)
-s SET   squeeze runs to one       (tr -s ' ' collapses repeated spaces)
-c       complement SET (all chars NOT in it)

Combine:  echo "one, two!" | tr -cs '[:alnum:]' '\n'  -> keeps alnum, turns every
other run into a single newline = one word per line.
Classes: [:upper:] [:lower:] [:digit:] [:alnum:] [:space:] [:punct:]
